caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1800 of 2009
lawyer:
A. B. Roy Chowdhury, Advocate instructed by Habibur Rahman Miah, Advocate-on-Record ---- For the Petitioners 
For the Respondents ----- None represented
parties:
Dilip Data and another ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Brahmanbaria and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
3. The defendant No. 1 contested case by filing written statement denying all the material allegations contending, inter-alia, that the trial Court recorded evidence and after hearing both the sides decreed the suit; that thereafter, the defendant preferred Title Appeal No.1-36 of 1998 in the Court of District Judge, Brahmanbaria; that the Joint District. Judge, 1st Court, Brahmanbaria heard the appeal, allowed the same and set aside the judgment of the trial Court; that thereafter, the revisional application was filed mainly on the grounds amongst others that the Court of Appeal below by misreading the evidence on record allowed the appeal with wrong findings and came to an erroneous decision causing failure of justice. It is the case of plaintiff that in the C.S. Khatian No. 545 in the relevant column it is shown that the suit Dag is a shahsan and it is a temple and a powerful committee sheba puja of the Hindu community but the Joint District Judge most illegally and arbitrarily found that there is no existence of any shashan and temple occasioning failure of justice. 

 "বিবাদী সরকার পক্ষ নালিশী ভূমি সংক্রান্ত ১ নং খাস খতিয়ান নং-এ হিসাবে চিহ্নিত করা হইয়াছে। উক্ত ১২৬৫ দাগে ভূমির শ্রেণী শ্বশ্মান হিসাবে উল্লেখ্ রহিয়াছে। নালিশী ভূমি স্থানীয় পরিদর্শক হয়। বগত কমিশনার তাহার প্রতিবেদনে উল্লেখ করেন যে, নালিশী ভূমিতে গম্বুজ বিশিষ্ট পুরাতন মন্দির আছে। এই অবস্থায় নালিশীভূমি শ্বশ্মান এই বিষয়ে বিতর্কের কোন অবকাশ নাই।" The learned Advocate further submitted that the High Court Division as well as the Court of Appeal below erred in law in discharging the Rule on non-reading and misreading of material evidence on record and on misconstruction of the important documents in the C.S. Khatian Ext. I which is mentioned as shisha, as such, the mere recording of the suit property as khan property is evidently wrong and without any foundation.
